records.title: Raj广大领土的贾达继承与南方例外（推演）

records.title: 1714年：Chandra Malhotra《On Honor》署注
records.description: Rayavhatimana理念将Wuhyun荣誉伦理引文署于Chandra Malhotra《On Honor》1714。作品讨论诚实、同伴与责任，没有声明该年创立独立Wuhyun国家。 此为已封存MOD理念的有年叙述，证据等级保持单一游戏文本；不自动修改政权、疆界或宗属。

dateEvidence.precision: explicit year in MOD narrative / diegetic quotation
dateEvidence.quote: 'To be Wuhyun is to be a man of honor, but what is honor? I answer you, honor is this: do not lie, do not be insincere, do not be obsequious, do not be superficial, do not be greedy, do not be rude, do not be boastful, do not be arrogant, do not slander, do not be unfaithful, be on good terms with comrades, do not be overly concerned with events, show concern for one another, be compassionate, with a strong sense of duty. To be Wuhyun is more than merely the swiftness of one’s blade or a willingness to lay down one's life.'\n-Chandra Malhotra, On Honor, 1714

records.title: 1818 Yodashikyu北Dhujat巩固反推
records.description: p19明确至1818控制北Dhujat大部；将固定1820 Yodashikyu中dhujat_region的非Sarisung省作为可关闭范围，扣除4501/4503既有1819跨区步骤后新增七省。省界只是本地地理标签与后期投影交集；shamakhad_region的4513/4524不在此步，因p30另有1823–1825北Kharunyana河岸战果的版本疑点。部分旧Xia空缺仅在1818重开，不倒填1812。

excerpts.19: 1814-1819: Yodashikyu invades Dhujat in order to further strengthen their position. Starting by attacking the exhausted and under-equipped Command garrison in Sarisung and seizing it by 1816 and invading the small warlords who occupied northern Dhujat. By 1818 Yodashikyu had secured most of northern Dhujar and laid siege to Portathi. This siege would be interrupted by the Command trying to attack Yodashikyu, leading to the siege being broken and Yodayikyu fighting the Command over northern Dhujat. The conflict would end in Yodashikyu’s favour with the Command being unable to push Yodashikyu out and hostilities cooling off by 1819.
excerpts.30: 1823-25: A skirmish between Yodashikyu and the Command results in Yodashikyu securing the northern bank of the Kharunyana from the Command. This disastrous defeat would be the nail in the coffin for the legitimacy of the Great Command and its rulers leading into the splintering of the Great Command.
